results.title: The role of metadata in reproducible computational research
results.content: # Review The role of metadata in reproducible computational research. The implementation of reproducible research for *in silico* analyses requires extensive metadata to describe both scientific concepts and the underlying computing environment. This review covers the wide range of metadata standards relevant to reproducible computational research across an “analytic stack” consisting of input data, tools, reports, pipelines, and publications. This review is designed to bridge the metadata and reproducible research communities. Reproducible computational research (RCR) is the keystone of the scientific method for *in silico* analyses, packaging the transformation of raw data to published results. This potential and wide support for the FAIR principles have motivated interest in metadata standards supporting reproducibility. Despite this shared connection with scientific data, few studies have explicitly described how metadata enable reproducible computational research. This review employs a functional content analysis to identify metadata standards that support reproducibility across an analytic stack consisting of input data, tools, notebooks, pipelines, and publications.

results.title: ENCORE: a practical implementation to improve ...
results.content: We presented ENCORE as a practical implementation, based on eight main requirements (Methods) and four practical principles (Supplementary Method 1, Section 2), guiding researchers on how to structure and document computational projects according to published guidelines5 1, 100099 (2020)."),19."),31."),32.") in order to improve transparency and reproducibility, and to improve harmonization within and across research groups. In addition, there are no requirements by design for further user and code documentation and the use of GitHub. Compared to the approach of Spreckelsen et al., ENCORE also aims to translate published guidelines into specific instructions and templates in, for example, the README Markdown files to guide researchers in making their computational work reproducible. ENCORE comprises a standardized file system structure (sFSS), pre-defined (Markdown) files for documentation, a GitHub repository for software version control, a HTML-based sFSS browser (sFSS Navigator), and ENCORE documentation to initiate a self-contained project compendium and support the researcher to use ENCORE in a consistent manner.
